topics.label: Introduction to the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture structure, learning objectives, and the framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and intracellular signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in receptor tyrosine kinase and Wnt/beta-catenin pathways enable cancer cells to achieve growth signal independence and resist inhibitory cues.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells arrest normal lineage differentiation programs across hematopoietic malignancies and intestinal epithelial tumors.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis, replicative senescence, and p53 stress responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells bypass intrinsic stress barriers like programmed cell death and telomere-mediated senescence through deregulation of p53 and telomerase activation.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the Warburg effect, tissue-specific metabolic changes, and how mutations in Krebs cycle enzymes generate oncometabolites that drive tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the angiogenic switch and the mechanisms by which expanding tumors stimulate new blood vessel growth to sustain nutrient and oxygen supply.

topics.label: Invasion, circulation, and the metastatic cascade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biological steps, clinical tracking, and genomic characteristics involved in cancer cell dissemination and colonization of distant sites.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecturer's concluding reflections on cancer hallmarks and closes the session.
